Understanding Agent Memory

Agent memory systems are crucial for maintaining context across interactions. This article explores different approaches to implementing memory in LLM-based agents.

The three main categories are: short-term memory, long-term memory, and episodic memory. Each serves a different purpose in the agent's cognitive architecture.

Short-term memory holds the current conversation context. Long-term memory stores persistent facts and preferences. Episodic memory captures specific past interactions that can be recalled when relevant.
